newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks rise at open despite falling golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks rise at open despite falling golds.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks climbed at the open as rising industrials, paper, real estate and pipelines offset falling golds. * Nine million shares traded worth C$172.1 million.
Toronto stocks opened higher on Wednesday as rising industrials, paper, real estate and pipelines offset sliding golds.
Traders said interest remained high in large capitalization stocks as investors sought safety in liquidity.
"I think for a lot of the smaller cap stocks there's definately ways of getting in, but it's very difficult to get out of them...there just isn't any bids," one trader said.
He said a weak gold sector was not enough to offset gains by most other Toronto sectors. Golds shed 108.90 points or 1.41 percent to 7589.18 in early trade.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 15.20 points to 6596.04 at the open in turnover of nine million shares worth C$172.1 million. Advances edged declines 222 to 219, while 215 issues traded flat.
Eleven of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes gained ground, led by the paper and forest products sector, which rose 60.87 points or 1.16 percent to 5306.31.
Conglomerates and merchandising joined gold on the losing side.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Shares in IPL Energy Inc rose 1.10 to 48.95 in moderate trade as investors approved of IPL's purchase of a 32 percent stake in Quebec holding company Noverco Inc.

* iStar internet inc rose 0.62 to 3.95 in early trade before settling back to 3.65. The company said on Tuesday it was "in negotiations with a major supplier, which, if completed, could have a possible impact on the company's business operations."
